newsitem.title: INDIA: India's Gujral hopes miffed TMC to join government.
newsitem.headline: India's Gujral hopes miffed TMC to join government.

text.p: Indian Prime Minister Inder Kumar said on Monday he was hopeful the disgruntled Tamil Maanila Congress (TMC) would join the new government.
"We are holding talks and are hopeful they will come around," Gujral told reporters after being being sworn in by President Shankar Dayal Sharma.

The TMC, miffed that its leader G.K. Moopanar was not chosen to lead the United Front, said on Saturday that it would not join the new government but would lend support to the alliance from outside. P. Chidambaram, the outgoing finance minister who belongs to the TMC, was not included in Gujral's cabinet.

The TMC's withdrawal raised doubts over the fate of the 1997/98 (April-March) budget that Chidambaram presented in February and which was due to be debated in a special session of parliament starting on Monday.
But United Front spokesman Jaipal Reddy said on Sunday he was confident Chidambaram would pilot the Finance Bill through parliament.
The Finance Bill gives effect to the tax and tariff proposals outlined in the budget.
